abi_boundary.disposition: crabc libc's public surface stays musl's and exports no mi_* symbol; every M7 external function is reachable only through the prefixed test adapter, which the gate evaluates.

differential:options-environment.scope: Separate pinned-C and Rust processes install the same environment images and compare every descriptor's name, legacy spelling, KiB unit, value, init state, and mi_option_get_size; the TID-normalized deprecated/invalid warning fragments in table order; the boolean-versus-mi_option_set store path (guarded coupling); the clamp, size, set_default, enable/disable, and out-of-range results; the complete mi_options_print_out output; the _mi_error_message gate (verbose bypass, show_errors, max_errors cap, error prefix), handler argument and code, and default errno result; and the thread-prefix formatting.

differential:adapter.scope: One unmodified C driver, linked once against the pinned C sources and once against the native `mi_*` adapter, runs the M7 option accessors and mutators (including invalid `mi_option_t` values and the guarded coupling), `mi_options_print_out`/`mi_options_print` through a registered output, `mi_register_error` with a handled and a default report (codes, argument, errno, and TID-normalized messages), `mi_register_deferred_free` through `mi_collect`, `mi_version`, and `mi_stats_get` (header validation, page counts around allocation, free, and collection, and a thread that has not initialized) and must print identical traces.

differential:deferred-free-callback.scope: Pinned C and Rust agree on deferred-free registration, generic-allocation heartbeat, force-on-OOM, owner-exit invocation, legal nested allocation, and recursion suppression.

differential:diagnostic-output-owner.scope: Pinned C and Rust agree on output registration, delayed-buffer flushing, NULL registration, post-init stderr routing, the warning cap, and final-statistics output.

differential:error-reporting-sites.scope: Pinned C and Rust report the same error code and message at each selected-source _mi_error_message site (for example oversized or overflowing allocation, invalid or double free, corrupted free lists, and arena/PageMap failures), and the libc boundary applies the default errno result.

differential:startup-page-map-failure.scope: One driver linked against pinned C and against the Rust native adapter lowers the address-space limit before process start so only the page-map reservation fails: startup completes with the page-map error in its delayed output, and every later small, zeroed, medium, large, huge, aligned, and realloc(NULL) request on the initial thread and on a worker fails with ENOMEM and the same error reports. Warnings are not compared (known-differences.md, CRABC-MI-STARTUP-PAGE-MAP-FAILURE).

differential:thread-init-failure.scope: One driver linked against pinned C and against the Rust native adapter: a worker whose thread-local-data or Theap metadata allocation fails reports the source out-of-memory and thread-initialization errors on each allocation attempt, fails that allocation with ENOMEM, keeps its thread running, and allocates normally once metadata is available again.

differential:option-effects.scope: For every descriptor with an allocator effect, a pinned-C/Rust trace in which mi_option_set before first use changes the same VM, arena, purge, reclaim, page-queue, and PageMap decision.

differential:reclaim-options.scope: Pinned C and Rust reach the same `mi_abandoned_page_try_reclaim` decision, page `used` count, and queue length for an own full page, foreign pages with an empty and a nonempty queue, and a large page, under environment profiles for the default, cross-thread (1) and disabled (-1) page_reclaim_on_free, zero page_max_reclaim and page_cross_thread_max_reclaim, and page_full_retain 0 and 5 (the Theap option image and the full-retain countdown).

differential:option-profiles.scope: Separate pinned-C and Rust processes per `mimalloc_*` environment image (disallow_arena_alloc, disallow_os_alloc, both, reserve_os_memory, and arena_reserve with default, lazy, and eager arena_eager_commit) report, for small, medium, large, and huge requests, whether each failed and the `mi_memkind_t` of its page, and the size and eager commitment of the arena backing a first small allocation.

differential:statistics.scope: Pinned-C/Rust mi_stats_* and mi_process_info values, JSON, and printed output for the selected MI_STAT level, normalized for addresses and times.

differential:visitation-profiles.scope: Pinned-C/Rust area/block visitation traces under the debug-padding, secure, and guarded profiles.

differential:debug-profile.scope: Pinned-C/Rust assertion, debug-fill, padding, and arena-print behavior of the MI_DEBUG/MI_SHOW_ERRORS/MI_PADDING profiles, with source-backed applicability for the sanitizer and tracking modes.

differential:secure-profile.scope: Pinned-C/Rust encoded free lists, guard pages, randomized allocation, and double-free/corruption detection under each MI_SECURE level and MI_FREE_IS_CHECKED.

differential:guarded-profile.scope: Pinned-C/Rust sampled guard-page allocation, guarded option effects, and Theap sample-rate/size-bound state under MI_GUARDED.

differential:optional-isa.scope: Pinned-C/Rust results of the MI_OPT_ARCH and MI_OPT_SIMD bitmap/allocation paths on a CPU that supports them.

audit:default-baseline.scope: The default x86-64 artifact keeps baseline x86_64-unknown-linux-musl target features and the release configuration image when every optional M7 profile is compiled out.

gates.acceptance: The complete `mi_options[]` table of src/options.c:112-177 (47 descriptors, release defaults, legacy spellings, KiB units) is one process image beside the output owner; `_mi_options_init` initializes it in table order after the verbose `process init` line, with each deprecated-spelling and invalid-value warning in source order and the warning cap applied after the loop; the environment grammar, boolean direct stores versus `mi_option_set` (guarded min/max coupling), UNINIT retry on an unavailable environment, the accessor and mutator semantics, and `mi_options_print_out` equal the pinned C behavior; raw `mi_option_t` values map to descriptors with the source out-of-range results.

Every descriptor with an allocator effect is read from the one process descriptor table at its source read point, so `mi_option_set` before first use changes later behavior exactly as in C. Deprecated descriptors, `os_tag` (a macOS-only Mach VM tag at src/prim/unix/prim.c:371), and `retry_on_oom` (read only by the Windows primitive) have no selected Linux effect; the guarded descriptors belong to m7.guarded.
blocked_by: The option-effects differential traces the arena max-object size, arena purge delay, minimal purge size, NUMA node count, generic-collect frequency, arena reservation size/eager commit, and `_mi_os_purge_ex` (purge_decommits, purge_delay, allow_reset) decisions after `mi_option_set`; the option-profile differential covers disallow_arena_alloc, disallow_os_alloc, reserve_os_memory, arena_reserve, and arena_eager_commit through process start and page allocation. page_commit_on_demand, arena_is_numa_local (a one-node host cannot discriminate it), reserve_huge_os_pages, reserve_huge_os_pages_at, destroy_on_exit, allow_thp's process THP policy, and allow_large_os_pages's large-page mapping branch have no decision-level C/Rust trace yet.

page_max_candidates (src/page.c:805), max_vabits (src/page-map.c:273), and pagemap_commit (src/page-map.c:299) are read from the process table at their source points but have no discriminating C/Rust trace: the reclaim profiles never build a queue of expandable, not-immediately-available pages, and no trace compares the PageMap reserved/committed extent under a configured max_vabits or a non-overcommit host.

gates.acceptance: Deferred-free heartbeat/force timing (src/page.c:987-1004) runs outside owner/engine/TLD/Theap projections; `mi_register_output` flushes the delayed buffer and switches routes as in src/options.c, delivering each source prefix and body as separate fragments; `mi_register_error` and every selected `_mi_error_message` site report through the source verbose/show_errors/max_errors gate and either call the registered handler or return the default errno result to libc's errno policy; `MI_XMALLOC` aborts on allocation failure.
blocked_by: Under the selected release flags (`-DMI_DEBUG=0 -DMI_SECURE=0 -DMI_GUARDED=0 -DMI_STAT=0`), the pinned preprocessor keeps 19 of the 37 `_mi_error_message` sites outside src/options.c; the other 18 (os.c:195, heap.c:51, arena.c:290,1047, alloc-posix.c:73, free.c:177,188,207,318,323,570,582,724,727, alloc.c:701,918, alloc-aligned.c:38, page-map.c:68) are compiled out and belong to the debug, secure, and guarded profiles. The error-site differential covers page.c:953,1063, alloc-aligned.c:83,165,192, and arena.c:1892 (the startup `reserve_os_memory` reservation). Of the rest, alloc.c:745 (`mi_try_new_handler`), reached through the adapter's `mi_new` family, and heap.c:79,138 and threadlocal.c:138 (first-class Heaps, owned by M6) are unported. The valid-program failure paths are ported: page-map.c:304 (a startup page-map reservation failure) leaves a started process whose every allocation fails with ENOMEM, as in C, covered by the startup-page-map-failure differential, with its unreproduced page-map commit warnings recorded as CRABC-MI-STARTUP-PAGE-MAP-FAILURE in `known-differences.md`; init.c:268 and theap.c:328 (thread-local-data and Theap metadata failures) follow C's lazy retry, covered by the thread-init-failure differential. libc.c:148 (`pthread_key_create` for the thread-done key) is not applicable: crabc libc drives thread finish directly and has no key to create. page.c:166,171 and arena.c:1457,1463,1476 are not applicable: they are reached only by an invalid program, and `known-differences.md` records the stricter Rust response as CRABC-MI-INVALID-PROGRAM-ERROR-SITES. libc keeps musl's errno for native allocation failures by the ABI decision, so the error handler and default errno are observable only through the native adapter.

gates.acceptance: The public `mi_stats_t` image and process-wide accessors of include/mimalloc-stats.h and src/stats.c (get, JSON, print, reset, bin sizes, `mi_process_info`) and every producer of the selected statistics level equal the pinned C values and output.
blocked_by: The native adapter maps only `mi_stats_get`; `mi_stats_get_json`, `mi_stats_as_json`, `mi_stats_print`, `mi_stats_print_out`, `mi_thread_stats_print_out`, `mi_stats_reset`, `mi_stats_get_bin_size`, and the `mi_process_info` family are absent, and `mi_stats_get` merges only the calling thread's default Theap on the process main subprocess.
Statistics producers gated on `MI_STAT > 0` are absent.

gates.acceptance: Heap, abandoned-page, Theap, and subprocess visitation (interfaces owned by M6) enumerate the source areas and blocks under every M7 profile, including debug padding, secure encoding, and guard pages, and visitor callbacks run outside owner/engine/TLD/Theap projections.
blocked_by: No area or block visitation exists, and no M7 profile exists to visit under.

gates.acceptance: Compile-time debug profiles select their own option defaults (for example `show_errors = 1` under `MI_DEBUG || MI_SHOW_ERRORS`), assertion levels, debug fill, and padding as in the pinned source; `mi_debug_show_arenas`/`mi_arenas_print` print the source arena image; sanitizer and tracking modes carry source-backed applicability decisions.
blocked_by: The engine selects only `DEBUG_LEVEL = 0` and `PADDING_SIZE = 0`; no debug, show-errors, or padding profile, assertion level, or debug fill exists.
`mi_debug_show_arenas` and `mi_arenas_print` are absent, including their prefixed test-adapter mapping.
No applicability decision exists for the TSAN/UBSAN and Valgrind/ASAN/ETW modes.

gates.acceptance: Each `MI_SECURE` level (encoded free lists, guard pages, randomized allocation, double-free and corruption detection) and `MI_FREE_IS_CHECKED` behave as the pinned source, including the `secure level` and free-list lines of `mi_options_print_out`.
blocked_by: The engine selects only `SECURE_LEVEL = 0`, unencoded free lists, and unchecked free.

gates.acceptance: The `MI_GUARDED` profile selects its guarded sample-rate default, samples guard-page allocations from the guarded options through `_mi_theap_guarded_init`, disables `allow_large_os_pages` with the source warning in `_mi_options_init`, and prints the guarded build line.
blocked_by: The engine selects only `GUARDED = false`; no guarded allocation path, Theap guarded state, or guarded option effect exists.

gates.acceptance: The optional `MI_OPT_ARCH` (x86-64 `-march=haswell -mavx2`) and `MI_OPT_SIMD` profiles are compile-time opt-in and produce the pinned C results on a CPU that supports them.
blocked_by: No optional ISA profile or `MI_OPT_SIMD` bitmap path exists.

gates.acceptance: With every optional M7 profile compiled out, the default x86-64 artifact keeps the baseline target features and release configuration; no M7 profile raises the baseline.
blocked_by: No default-artifact target-feature and configuration audit exists.
